answer.rationale: Finance has mandathed a steep 18% component spend reduction this year, and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle. Memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, and onboarding was quick with clean invoicing — directy supporting the cut-cost goal and reducing execution risk on a 14-day clock. Memory_c6 shows a longer-term lever (multi-year commitment unlocking volume pricing) but requires a commitment the incumbent will not currently honor and does not solve the immediate gap alone. Pulling both lets me confirm the low-cost vendor economics and invoicing accuracy from a recent, verified record before locking the switch. Given the line is running at 94% with no buffer, I intend to switch_primary_vendor as a small, guarded test order (not full immediate transition) to confirm quality and continuity before scaling, preserving uncertainty rather than treating the memory evidence as guaranteed.
